model.description: Provider model id; the template carries ctx.model (strict, resolved at instantiation). Convention (K-H2): pass a RESOLVED literal. The summarizer's writer reads the SAME key - give it a cheaper model per instance via override_params on summarizer/writer.

description.purpose: The agent's brain: the one inference of the composite. It answers the assembled context the collector hands it over the seam, and its system state - identity, instructions, tool schemas, the memory bundle, the handover of the last closed generation - accumulates in its own cell.db, one writer per path.
description.use_when: Inside the talky composite. The seam edge (collector -> here) carries the iteration bound and restore_ttl; the answer edge (here -> split) carries stop and tool_calls, and the split decides which of the two it is.
description.not_in_scope: No tool execution, no context assembly, no persona of its own beyond what is seeded or written into it. Provider and auth are instance business: the shipped default is the OpenRouter chat lane, a subscription or another provider is override_params.
description.emits_meaning: finish_reason 'stop'/'tool_calls' -> ./dispatcher (the dispatcher tells a final answer from a tool bundle); 'length' -> the collector's in_answer lane (a truncated answer is an answer); 'error'/'content_filter' -> ./errors, because an error echo carries the PROMPT back and must never be filed as the agent's own words.
description.consumes_meaning: messages[] the assembled context of one turn (window, memory bundle, tool round). A body with system but WITHOUT messages is a system update: it upserts the slot and triggers no inference - that is how the summarizer's handover arrives, which is why the messages slot is not required here.
examples: assembled turn -> tool_calls -> the round runs -> the same seam again with iter+1 -> stop
system.handover update after a close -> the slot is replaced, no provider call
